> 1)I receive this error message: Error in names(range_probabilities) = ranges_list :
>  'names' attribute [11] must be the same length as the vector [8]

You need to get ranges_list to be of length 11, so look at the line setting it up. This seems to say it has length 8. You could just manually write it out:

ranges_list = c("_",  "S",  "I",  "A",  "O",  "SI", "SA", "SO", "IA", "IO", "AO")

> 2)When the names of possible ranges show up on the screen, there is a blank range at the beginning: ranges_list
>  [1] "_"  "S"  "I"  "A"  "O"  "SI" "SA" "SO" "IA" "IO" "AO"

That's the null range, that is expected behavior under defaults (where include_null_range=TRUE)

Cheers!

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Re: Sample size -> AICc
messages.body_plain:
Yep, sample size should be the number of tips in the tree.  Another, non-phylogenetic, model would be to draw the ranges randomly from a hat, and again the sample size would be the number of ranges you've observed.  We just typically use phylogenetic models because we think evolution has something to do with explaining our data  ;-).
Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: Interpreting results: what questions should I be asking?
messages.subject_clean: Interpreting results: what questions should I be asking?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

This is the first time I've used `BioGeoBEARS`, and I'm still learning how the package works, including how the models work and what the different free parameters mean. I'm in the exploratory phase, trying to reconstruct ancestral biogeographic ranges on a global scale. I have a time-scaled phylogenetic tree and a `geogfn` table, nothing more. I just ran my data twice, once using the DEC model (top) and once using the DEC+J mode (bottom). The LnL for the DEC+J is considerably better, and quite a few nodes have different results. (I also noticed that two of the parameters--d and e--both have a value of 0 under the DEC+J model. Is that fishy?)

My question, which is unfortunately somewhat broad, is, what now? What questions should I be asking?

Should I compare these two using the LRT? Should I run more models (all the models?) and compare them using the AIC? Should I try adding extra parameters, such as distance? I'd appreciate it if someone gave me some statistical guidance. It's the theory that I don't necessarily understand, and I'm not sure what specific questions I should be asking. I apologize in advance for my ignorance.

Hi -- briefly, your first task is to get a newick file that will load with the ape package. It looks like you are trying to load something that is not a newick tree file.

library(ape)
trfn = "put_the_actual_file_name_here.newick"
tr = read.tree(trfn)
plot(tr)
axisPhylo()

...get this to work before trying anything else in R or BioGeoBEARS...

(And, google what a newick file is, if you don't know!)

Cheers,
Nick

On Thu, Feb 28, 2019 at 10:53 AM <mayko...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello everyone,
>
> This is my first attempt at any biogeography project. Whenever I try to use the command trfn="my tree file name" I receive the error "Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : attempt to set index 61/60 in SET_STRING_ELT".
>
> I don't have any branch lengths of zero, and I am unsure what this error means.
>
> Any feedback is appreciated!
>
> Best,
>
> Tyler Maykovich
